html:
A New Year statement of 1 January 1946 in which Emperor Hirohito of Japan denied that he was a living god. The American occupation authorities asked for it after Japan's defeat in the Second World War.

Since the Meiji Restoration, the state had taught that the emperor descended from the sun goddess Amaterasu, and State Shinto tied worship at shrines to loyalty to the throne. The rescript said the bond between emperor and people rested on trust and affection, not on myths, and not on the idea that the Japanese were a race above others.

Its wording was careful. It opened by quoting the Charter Oath of 1868, and Hirohito later said that restating that oath was its main point. Still, it opened the way for the Constitution of Japan, which made the emperor a symbol of the state with no political power. Shinto shrines carried on as private religious bodies, cut off from the state.
